column1: # Short-read QC thresholds (python/short_read_qc.py). PROVISIONAL: conservative starting points, not universal cut-offs.
# Set them from pilot data on the intended sequencing platform and organisms, then mark every row `frozen` and record the
# file's hash (it is written to every QC row as thresholds_sha) BEFORE the main benchmark is run. Do not tune them against
# which tool wins. direction min: the metric must not fall below the limit; max: must not rise above it.
# warn: the sample proceeds, flagged. reject: the sample is excluded from the primary benchmark when SHORT_READ_QC_MODE=enforce.
# A blank reject means there is no rejection limit for that metric. Integrity failures (unreadable, truncated, empty, malformed
# FASTQ, unequal read counts) always reject and are not listed here.

column6: Fewer pairs cannot cover a bacterial genome at useful depth.
Uses the genome size given, or 5 Mb when not given (flagged genome_size_assumed). Plasmid recovery needs depth beyond the chromosome's.
Mean Phred of the sampled bases.
Share of bases at Q30 or better.
Median over the shorter mate; very short reads assemble poorly.
Reads carrying an adapter: stage 3 trims them, so only a large share is a concern.
Read with caution: very high depth also duplicates reads.
Read names that disagree between R1 and R2 at the same position: the files are out of sync.
Absolute GC difference from the expected organism GC; only evaluated when --expected-gc is given.
